title: os dev's in-place upgrade says every refused database is "still in the v17 organization-ownership shape", after an ERROR-level stack dump of the boot refusal — an 18.0 pre-release database (and a database HEAD itself created) is told it is v17
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect (user-visible, stable reproduction, named location; shipped CLI text — the "frozen at release" exception applies).

- Category: ① — reach: `os dev` from an app directory whose `.objectstack/data/objectstack.db` an 18.0.0-next.5 `os dev` created, measured once at 307ce4c4.
- Who acts: the seat that owns `packages/cli` `os dev` (the 18.x organization-ownership line, follow-up to PR #24681) — `packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts` (the recover branch, ~line 822) and the refused child's log output.
- Dedup: local scan of the 625 newest issues (state=all, open and closed) for `v17 organization-ownership shape|still in the v17|os dev.*upgrad` — 0 hits; for `birth|ownership|ceremony` — 25 hits, none on this text. Related, not the same: #24827 (a fresh HEAD database refused, where this line also appears) and #24638 (the `[schema-drift]` line that prescribes `--allow-destructive` for `organization_id`, still printed in the same boot).

reach: `os dev` (nothing chosen) over an 18.0.0-next.5 development database, 307ce4c4.
Path: cli.dev-boot-contract
QA-source: #24838 · cli.dev-boot-contract · observed beside the clauses (upgrade matrix cell d)
Checklist item priority: P0
type: Bug

## Reproduction (framework 307ce4c4)

1. In a scratch copy of `examples/app-showcase` taken at the `@objectstack/cli@18.0.0-next.5` tag (`820fd5aef0`), run that release's `os dev --seed-admin -p PORT` with no database chosen. It creates `.objectstack/data/objectstack.db`. Use it (sign in, invite and sign up a member, create a task), then stop it.
2. Replace the app's code with HEAD's `examples/app-showcase` and keep `.objectstack/`. Run HEAD's `os dev --seed-admin -p PORT`.
3. What the developer sees, in order:
   - two `[schema-drift] sys_secret.organization_id / sys_flow_credential.organization_id: column exists … (orphaned) — "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.` lines (the drop gate refuses that command for these columns; the ceremony drops them — #24638);
   - `ERROR Plugin startup failed: com.objectstack.organization-ownership-boot-guard {"error":{"message":"This database carries no organization-ownership marker: 17.x or an 18.0 pre-release (18.0.0-next.*) created it …","stack":"OrganizationOwnershipBootRefusal: … at assertOrganizationOwnershipMigrated …` plus a `[Kernel] Plugin startup failed: …` line and about ten `at …` stack frames;
   - then `⟳ This development database is still in the v17 organization-ownership shape — upgrading it in place (a copy is kept first)…` and `✓ Upgraded the development database to the v18 organization ownership …`.
4. Expected: one plain account of what happened — this database was created by an 18.0 pre-release (or 17.x), `os dev` is upgrading it in place, and here is the copy. Actual: the line names the wrong origin ("v17") and comes after an ERROR line with a stack trace for a refusal `os dev` handles itself.

The upgrade itself is correct: the copy is kept under `.objectstack/data/backups/organization-ownership-TIMESTAMP/`, the ceremony completes, the 18.0 users sign in with their old passwords and read their own data.

The same "v17" sentence is printed for a database HEAD created itself when the first command was `os migrate apply` (#24827), so on this release the sentence is wrong in every case the record met.

## Where

- `packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts` ~822: the `recover` branch prints the v17 sentence unconditionally. The refusal it reacts to (`organizationOwnershipRefusalMessage`, `packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`) already says "17.x or an 18.0 pre-release", and the IPC message (`ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_REQUIRED_MESSAGE`) carries the tables.
- The ERROR line and stack come from the kernel's plugin-start failure log in the `serve --dev` child, printed before the child sends the IPC message that `os dev` recovers from.
